title: Kansas police chief used Flock license plate cameras 164 times to track ex-girlfriend

reading.body:
This is not a failure of the licence plate reader's recognition. It is an insider misuse of a deployed system, where a person with legitimate access used it for a purpose it was never built for. The misuse happened at the query layer, in the account of the officer running the searches, not in the cameras or the matching software.

The searches were evidently recorded, since a count of them exists in the certification order. What was missing was review of those records against a policing purpose, and any check that would flag repeated queries about one private individual by a single officer. Auditing query logs for searches with no case attached, or for subjects connected to the officer, is the kind of control that would have surfaced this early rather than after months of use.

The headline and the certification order give different counts of the searches, and which figure is accurate is not established here. Whether any criminal charge followed the resignation and the loss of certification is also not established. The order is a finding by a state certification body, not a court verdict.

reports.title: Kansas police chief used Flock license plate cameras 164 times to track ex-girlfriend

summary: From June to October 2023, Sedgwick, Kansas, Police Chief Lee Nygaard reportedly used Flock Safety license plate readers 228 times to check where his ex-girlfriend and her new boyfriend were, according to a Kansas certification order. The order said he also followed them in a police vehicle and admitted jealousy influenced his conduct. Nygaard resigned in October 2023, and later lost his police certification.
